newsitem.title: UK: GA PREDICTS HEALTHY GROWTH FOR LIFE ARM.
newsitem.headline: GA PREDICTS HEALTHY GROWTH FOR LIFE ARM.

text.p: British insurer General Accident on Tuesday ruled out an imminent acquisition in the life sector but predicted its life operations would continue the healthy growth seen in the first half.

"We've got to get the full benefits of the Provident Mutual acquisition. We'll concentrate on getting that nailed down and then move on and look at other options," chief executive Bob Scott told Reuters.

"We have a pretty good base for organic growth and that's a very good investment for shareholders... We believe the level of growth achieved in the first six months should at least be maintained for the rest of year."

Life profits rose 37 percent in the first half of 1997 to 63 million pounds. The advance reflected not only the absence of integration costs but also the benefits of focusing on growing the business, said Scott.
As well as growth in profits, new business was also up and more importantly, profitable, he added.
Group operating profits for the first half climbed to a record 260 million pounds, toward the top end of analyst forecasts, up from 193 million pounds last year.
But general insurance remains difficult and highly competitive in all GA's major territories.
The focus going forward would be on maintaining underwriting worldwide and growing the life business, said Scott.

While the UK produced an "outstanding" underwriting profit of 19 million pounds, he said, it was increasingly hard to get rate increases and to some extent that reflected the position in most countries.
"The U.S. has been on a long down cycle which it doesn't seem to be able to shake off -- there's pressure on rates there continually. Canada is difficuilt too. There's nowhere to hide."
There were definite signs of rate increases being applied by a number of companies in UK private motor, but not in other product lines.
"We've had very favourable weather in the UK for some time so results look a lot better than they would if you averaged out the weather over the period," said Scott.
Increases in personal and commercial premiums by GA had stuck but it had lost some business in commercial as a result of the rise.
"We tried last year to get increases in personal and couldn't get them. This year we're probably more in tune with the rest of the market," added Scott.
UK subsidence costs increased 50 percent to 12 million stg in the first half and a similar increase is expected over the full year.
In the U.S. it was proving very hard to get rate increases, said Scott.

GA was vigorously attacking the homeowners account which has been very poorly performing and was also putting rate increase on commercial property, according to Scott, but private motor remained very good.
An improved underwriting result was recorded in the U.S., reflecting reduced severe weather costs.
